title: RichBlock
description: One block of a rich assistant message (master plan 14.1): markdown, code, table, chart, diagram, citation_list, action_card, clarification_choices or confirmation_panel, discriminated by type. Blocks are data, never executable HTML or JavaScript: no block has a URL, a path, an expression, a script, a callback or an HTML member, and every fixed-shape object forbids additional properties. Free content (markdown text, code, table cells, chart data, diagram source) is 'model' authority: it is verified against the DialogueDirective, sanitised in the core (M3-05) and treated as untrusted by the renderer. Blocks that present application state (action_card, confirmation_panel, citation_list, clarification_choices) are assembled by the core from PreparedActions, ActionReceipts, citations and adapter results, so their identifying and factual members are 'alixai' or 'host'. The host application decides which renderers are enabled; a client that does not support a type shows the text alternative.

plainText.title: Plain text
plainText.description: A string with no HTML tag start: a '<' may not be followed by a letter, '/', '!' or '?'. Defence in depth for strings a renderer might otherwise be tempted to inject into markup. It does not replace sanitisation in the core or text-only rendering in the client; '<18' and 'a < b' remain valid.

markdownBlock.description: Markdown text. Text only: no raw HTML is honoured and sanitisation happens in the core (M3-05) before the block is emitted.

codeBlock.description: A code listing, shown verbatim and never executed.

language.description: Language hint for highlighting, lower case, for example python or c++.

tableBlock.description: A table of plain values. Every row has one cell per column, in column order; the renderer treats every cell as text.

rows.description: Row data. Each row is an array of cells in column order.

key.description: Stable column key, a field name.

kind.description: Formatting hint for the cells of the column.

chartBlock.description: A restricted, declarative chart: the data is inline, the mark comes from a fixed enum and encodings name data fields. There is no URL, no expression, no transform, no aggregate and no HTML, so the chart is exactly reproducible from the data it declares. Every encoded field must exist in the data (checked by the core, not expressible here). The data must not hide an unverified application fact: figures that state application facts are checked against the DialogueDirective like any other claim.

description.description: Text alternative that states what the chart shows. Required: it is what a client without a chart renderer, a screen reader and the verifier use.

data.description: Inline data: an array of records, each a flat object of scalar values keyed by field name. Never a URL.

encoding.description: Which data field drives which visual channel.

chartRecord.description: One data record: a flat object of scalars keyed by field name.

chartScalar.description: A chart data value. Strings are plain text.

chartEncoding.description: Channel to field mappings. A cartesian mark (bar, line, area, point) uses x and y and may add color; a pie uses theta and color. Channels hold a field name and a type, never an expression.

field.description: The data field the channel reads.

type.description: How to read the field: nominal (unordered categories), ordinal (ordered categories), quantitative (numbers) or temporal (dates and times).

diagramBlock.description: A diagram as typed text. The block carries Mermaid source and is flagged as needing a host renderer: AlixAI never renders it and ships no renderer. Schema-level guards reject Mermaid's front matter, %%{ }%% directives (which can loosen the renderer's security level), click and link statements (callbacks and URLs) and javascript: text; the host's renderer must still run Mermaid in its strict security mode.

language.description: The diagram language. Only mermaid is defined.

requires_host_renderer.description: Always true: the host application must render this block or fall back to the text alternative.

description.description: Text alternative that states what the diagram shows.

citationListBlock.description: The sources supporting an answer, one Citation each.

citations.description: The citations, from the core's RAG service.

actionCardBlock.description: A structured application result or an offer of next steps: a title, canonical facts and the actions the user may take. Built from adapter results and ActionReceipts.

title.description: Canonical card title from the host application.

capability_id.description: The capability the card concerns, if any.

facts.description: The facts shown on the card.

actions.description: The next steps the user may take from the card.

preparation_id.description: The PreparedAction the card relates to, if any.

receipt_id.description: The ActionReceipt the card reports, if any.

clarificationChoicesBlock.description: A clarification the user answers by selecting one choice. The same payload is carried by the clarification TurnEvent. Selecting a choice sends its choice_id; allow_free_text says whether the user may instead type an answer, which is then validated like any other turn.

field.description: The capability field the clarification asks for.

prompt.description: The question as the model worded it. Optional: a client may render its own wording from field. Verified against the directive's next_question before it is emitted.

answer_kind.description: choice: pick a listed value. entity: pick the record the user meant from the candidates the host returned.

allow_free_text.description: True when the user may type an answer instead of selecting.

choices.description: The selectable answers, from the capability contract or the host's candidates.

confirmationPanelBlock.description: The confirmation of a PreparedAction: the canonical summary, the exact effects, the risk level, the expiry and how it may be confirmed. Rendered from the PreparedAction by the core, so the user confirms what the host validated and not what the model said. A panel exists only when confirmation is required.

preparation_id.description: The PreparedAction being confirmed. The confirmation call is bound to it.

effects.description: The exact effects and their targets.

risk_level.description: Effective risk level of the action.

expires_at.description: When the preparation, and so the confirmation, expires.

confirmation.description: How the action may be confirmed. explicit or step_up only.
